title: SLO-cost-curves-gpu-recommendations-wip
content:
Purpose: quick working notes for SLO-driven cost vs perf curves. Aim is to produce a simple recommendation map (by SLO tier) for which GPU class to prioritize in Optimize and Dedicated capacity proposals. This doc intentionally mixes rough numbers, assumptions, and next steps — not final pricing.

Scope and test assumptions
- Synthetic workload: decoder-only 7B-class evaluation model (7B dense transformer), context 1024, average generation length 64 tokens. This is representative of lightweight chat/assistant backends we commonly route to for low-latency flows.
- Quantization: fv4/q4_0 baseline for A100/H100, q8 for A10/L4 unless noted.
- Batch strategy: continuous small batching (2-8 requests) for interactive; large batching (up to 64) for throughput tests.
- Power draw numbers are measured system-level averages from lab runs (card + host under test load); not TDP spec values.

Single-GPU baseline numbers (lab sweep, median of 3 runs)
- Columns: instance | measured tokens/sec | est power draw (W) | tokens/sec per W | price (usd/hr) | est $/token
- A10   | 190 t/s |  85 W  | 2.24 t/s/W | $0.60/hr | $0.00000088
- L4    | 320 t/s | 120 W  | 2.67 t/s/W | $1.40/hr | $0.00000122
- A100  | 700 t/s | 250 W  | 2.80 t/s/W | $3.20/hr | $0.00000127
- H100  | 1620 t/s| 420 W  | 3.86 t/s/W | $9.00/hr | $0.00000154

Notes on the numbers above
- $/token = price_per_hour / (tokens/sec * 3600). These are single-GPU nominal numbers; real cluster pricing (reserved/dedicated) will materially change absolute $/token but relative order generally holds for similar reservation discounts.
- A10 looks cheapest per token in this micro-benchmark for the 7B-class model because the model fits easily and batching inefficiencies are low; H100 gives best perf/W but higher $/hr pulls $/token back up for this model size.
- L4 sits in a sweet spot for low-latency interactive workloads: better latency than A10, lower cost than A100 for modest batch sizes.

SLO-driven recommendations (rough)
- Low-latency SLOs (p95 < 50 ms): prioritize L4 or H100 for hot routes. H100 only justified for high QPS with aggressive concurrency because of high hourly cost; L4 is often more cost-effective for p95-sensitive ~50–200 RPS workloads.
- Conservative-cost interactive (p95 50–200 ms): A10 can be primary for sparse, low-throughput routes (QPS < 20) and for off-peak traffic; recommend A10 pool with autoscale-to-L4 when p95 starts trending up.
- Throughput-first batch jobs (no strict latency): A100 is recommended for large batch inference where sequence lengths and model size push utilization higher; A100 amortizes cost well when batch sizes > 16 and model size >=13B.

Operational tradeoffs
- Cold-start & memory fragmentation: A100/H100 reduce sharding and model-split overheads for >13B models. For 7B-class, fragmentation is minimal and smaller cards (A10/L4) are attractive.
- Energy considerations: H100 yields best perf/W but only matters when unit-price of electricity and thermal provisioning constraints come into play (private deployments). For cloud-hosted we show perf/W as an observability metric but decisions are primarily $/token.
- Quantization sensitivity: q4_0 on A100/H100 gives big cost savings for larger models. We need per-model quantization regressions to maintain quality guardrails.

Example decision matrix (how to pick by route)
- Route: chat-short (avg resp 32 tokens, SLO p95 70ms) -> prefer L4 (burstable to H100 if spikes)
- Route: assistant-long (avg resp 256 tokens, tolerant p95 300ms) -> prefer A100 (batching allowed)
- Route: low-volume personalization (QPS < 5, p95 < 250ms) -> prefer A10 (cost-first)

Open questions / unresolved
- Dedicated/reserved pricing tiers: need to rerun the calc with committed-rate discounts (10%, 25%, 40%) for each GPU class to show break-even points.
- Multi-GPU model sharding overhead for 13B+ on L4 pools (OOM and cross-GPU sync penalties). Lab tests incomplete.
- Real workload token distribution: our synthetic 64/256 split needs to be validated against production route histograms (ask product for sampled traces).
- SLA-driven fallback policy: should we implement automatic fallback from H100->A100->L4 when capacity pressure occurs? Need SRE input on latency tail impact.

Suggested next steps (action items)
- EVAN: run reserved pricing sensitivity sweep (10/25/40% off) and append a cost-breakout table per-GPU by discount tier (due 2025-12-01).
- SOFIA: collect production token-length histograms for top 10 customer routes (due 2025-11-10).
- RAHUL: test q4_0 vs q8 on L4 for 13B model to measure quality delta and perf delta (due 2025-11-20).
- PR: add perf/W telemetry to the Optimize dashboard (small card under instance economics) and wire up to per-route cost breakdown (design ticket linked above).

Quick appendices (raw math examples)
- A10 tokens/hr = 190 * 3600 = 684,000 -> $/token = 0.60 / 684,000 = 8.77e-7
- H100 tokens/hr = 1620 * 3600 = 5,832,000 -> $/token = 9.00 / 5,832,000 = 1.54e-6

Stylistic notes (for reviewers)
- This is intentionally engineering-facing and slightly rough. Numbers are lab medians; do not copy into customer proposals without reserved pricing and model-specific reruns.
- Goal is to produce a small set of clear recommendations for the Optimize product page and the Dedicated capacity sizing playbook.

Questions for reviewers
- Product: do we want a client-visible ‘recommended instance’ badge per route (sized by SLO)?
- Eng: are there objections to continuing to treat L4 as our preferred latency-first cost option for 7B-class models?


End of notes.
